newsitem.title: GREECE: New Greek Eurobank set to operate in early 1997.
newsitem.headline: New Greek Eurobank set to operate in early 1997.

text.p: Greece's new Eurobank, the offspring of a merger between private Eurobank and Interbank will be ready to operate under its new organisational and management structure in the first few months of 1997, it said in a statement.
Eurobank belongs to the Latsis group of banks which bought 95 percent of private Interbank from Banque Worms via Consolidated Eurofinance Holdings SA last July it said.
Consolidated Eurofinance Holdings is Eurobank's mother company.
George Gontikas will be the president of Eurobank and Nickolaos Nanopoulos its managing director under its new management and operational structure, it said.
Eurobank will have three general directorates with Vyron Ballis heading retail banking, Christos Sorotos at the helm of operations and Haris Kyrkos heading wholesale banking, it said.

Eurobank plans to develop international activities in treasury, private banking and venture capital in cooperation with other banks belonging to the Latsis group and aims at becoming an international bank with strong presence in the greater Balkan area, it added.

The new Eurobank had assets of 560 billion drachmas, equity capital of 45 billion drachmas, a network of 32 branches that is projected to exceed 40 in 1997, served 150,000 clients and employed 900 persons as of December 1996, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
